skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Generate short cinematic videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through the RunComfy CLI. It documents input schema, prompt patterns, reference media limits, and model routing guidance.
skill.summary: Run RunComfy Seedance 2.0 Pro workflows for short multimodal videos.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and documented schema examples. Confirmed issues are the intended RunComfy CLI execution and outbound requests to RunComfy model endpoints. No prompt injection, malware intent, or unauthorized filesystem access was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on external RunComfy CLI execution.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before installing or running the CLI, and show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: The setup flow recommends global package installation.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned CLI version or document how to verify the package before global installation.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media references are sent to a third-party model API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential prompts, private media URLs, or regulated data unless approved.

content.value_statement: Short video prompts often fail when references, duration, and audio limits are unclear. This skill provides RunComfy Seedance 2.0 Pro commands, schema guidance, and prompt patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose Seedance 2.0 Pro over related video models.
Shows RunComfy CLI commands for text-only and reference-based video generation.
Documents supported inputs for prompts, images, videos, audio, duration, resolution, and aspect ratio.
Provides prompt guidance for camera motion, identity references, audio tone, and lip sync.
Lists operational limits, exit codes, token storage, and outbound RunComfy endpoints.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access to the RunComfy Model API.
The documented endpoint only supports 4 to 15 second clips.
The playground variant is limited to 720p output.
Generated quality depends on reference media and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Create short advertising clips
use_cases.description: Plan Seedance prompts that combine product context, camera direction, and natural audio for short marketing videos.

use_cases.title: Prototype cinematic scenes
use_cases.description: Turn references and scene notes into concise RunComfy inputs for film previs and social video tests.

use_cases.title: Evaluate multimodal video settings
use_cases.description: Compare prompt, image, video, and audio reference choices before running a Seedance job.

prompt_templates.title: Create a text-only clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a simple Seedance generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Seedance 2.0 Pro to make a 5 second 9:16 video about [scene]. Include camera motion and audio tone.

prompt_templates.title: Add an image reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for stable identity or brand visuals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Seedance prompt using [image reference] for stable identity. Put action, mood, lighting, and spoken tone in the prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Combine media references
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for image, video, and audio reference planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multimodal Seedance job with [image], [video], and [audio]. Separate identity, scene motion, and voice guidance clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Design a variant test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for repeatable creative testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three Seedance variants for [campaign]. Keep subject and duration fixed, then vary camera motion, audio tone, and lighting.

output_examples.input: Create a 5 second cafe ad with a warm speaker and gentle ambience.
output_examples.output: A concise Seedance prompt with medium close-up framing, slow push-in motion, warm window light, friendly voice, and 9:16 settings.

output_examples.input: Use a headshot and voice reference for a product update.
output_examples.output: A production brief that places stable identity in image references and places script, tone, and camera direction in the prompt.

output_examples.input: Compare Seedance with Wan for an audio-led lip sync task.
output_examples.output: A routing recommendation that selects Wan for user-owned driving audio and Seedance for native generated dialogue.

best_practices: Use image references for stable identity, logos, costumes, and other fixed visual details.
Keep prompts focused on action, camera motion, lighting, mood, and audio tone.
Match reference media aspect ratios to the target output when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not describe a face in long text when an image reference is available.
Do not mix conflicting style references in the same generation request.
Do not request clips longer than the documented 15 second endpoint limit.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It documents RunComfy CLI commands for the ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro model endpoint.

faq.question: Does it generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. The RunComfy CLI sends the request to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: What reference media can I use?
faq.answer: The documented schema supports image, video, and audio references within the listed count and duration limits.

faq.question: Can it create long videos?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents a 4 to 15 second duration range for this endpoint.

faq.question: Does it support lip sync?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers native generated audio and prompt patterns for natural lip sync.

faq.question: What should I avoid submitting?
faq.answer: Avoid confidential prompts, private media URLs, and regulated data unless your organization approves RunComfy use.
